text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- A document put together by experts working for the parliamentary commission investigating the Tocsik scandal says the general staff of the State Privatisation & Holding Co. was under political pressure, mediated by then privatisation minister Tamas Suchman.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny said there could be an average 18 percent salary increase in the health sector.
- Free Democrat party president Ivan Peto was reelected on Sunday as head of the parliamentary group.
- Laszlo Kover, a Young Democrat vice president, said the question is which of the two leading opposition parties - the Smallholders and the Young Democrats - will won the 1998 elections.
- The credit-rating agency Moody's improved its grading of three Hungarian commercial banks to Ba1 last Thursday.
- Hungary's first 24-hour shopping channel will go on the air for cable subscribers in early March.
- Police today will start clamping wheel locks on illegally parked vehicles in downtown Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG

- According to a recent Sonda-Ipsos poll Smallholders' Party topped the poll with suport from 26 percent of decided voters, followed by the Young Democrats with 25 percent and the governing Socialists third with 22 percent. The Free Democrats also hit a new low with 9 percent, followed by the Christian Democrats with 6 percent, the Democratic Forum with 5 percent.
- The heads of state of the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia are to meet for a summit in Gniezno, Poland on June 3.
- The State Audit Office has uncovered costly inefficiencies and irregularities in support given by the State Privatisation & Holding Co to the steel industry in Borsod.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament will start debating the bills on conflicts of interest and an amendment to the privatisation law on Feb 25.

- A senior official at the Welfare Ministry has outlined some details of a new pension concept under which individuals will have to pay more social insurance contribution from next January, while the employers' contribution will be lowered from the present 39 percent.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Hungary's economic indices are unlikely to improve considerably this year or in 1998, said Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy at a finance conference on Friday. According to Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institution, an efficient banking system is an indispensable prerequisite to any country's economic growth. (Sat.)
- The balance of payments deficit fell to $1.7 billion last year, according to preliminary figures from the National Bank.
- Industrial production prices rose by 1 percent in December last year, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The tourism sector will receive a HUF 4 billion in development funds this year.
- Hypo Bank Rt. and its brokerage and leasing firm generated a HUF 610 million pre-tax profit last year. (Sat.)
- Private investors oversubscribed the HUF 700 million share package issued by Realbank Rt. by HUF 305 million.
- The national railway firm MAV will demand that its Czech counterpart reimburse MAV for HUF 40 million losses incurred by the Czech railway strike.
- The Forum Hotel recorded a HUF 1 billion pre-tax profit last year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
